note: Adapted from Light & Wilson 1936, original in English (The nasute termites of the Philippines, The Philippine Journal of Science 60: 461–520). Both the alate and the worker are given as Unknown in the original; a single lot, collected by Taylor on the coast of Cotabato, Mindanao, type collection No. 1154; biology unknown. Fig. 18 (soldier head in dorsal and lateral view, left mandible) not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Head pale yellow, nasus pale red, abdominal tergites pale yellow and very weakly sclerotized; outline in dorsal view concave (although there is a slight nasus peak); front of the head concave; apex of the nasus slightly upturned; antennae 12-segmented, segments 2 and 3 subequal.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head dark yellow; nasus pale red; abdominal tergites pale yellow, very weakly sclerotized. Head and nasus shape as in Fig. 18 a, b: outline in dorsal view concave, although there is a slight nasus peak; front of the head concave; apex of the nasus slightly upturned. Head covered with a layer of long fine white hairs and a few scattered bristle-like hairs. Left mandible as in Fig. 18 c. Antennae 12-segmented, about five sevenths as long as head plus nasus, segments 2 and 3 subequal. Measurements (mm and indices, from type collection No. 1154, a typical soldier from Cotabato, Mindanao): head plus nasus 1.62; head length (excluding nasus) 0.96; nasus length 0.66; head projection 0.24; head height 0.66; head width 1.02; fore tibia length 0.72; head index 1.06; head-nasus index 0.69; head projection index 0.25; leg extension index 0.75.
